home.subtitle: TUNCIS 2026 brings together on October 23–24, 2026 in Sousse an intentionally small community (places are limited) around a dual ambition.
home.para1: Reconnect Tunisian research, locally and internationally. Many Tunisian researchers work today in European laboratories, often at the highest level of their discipline, and maintain ties with colleagues back home that are more affective than operational. TUNCIS aims to transform these ties into real collaborations.
home.para2: Bridge research and industrial practice. Between a published result and an AI system actually running in production, the gap remains considerable.

cfc.title: Transform Your Research into Impact
cfc.intro: Are you working on an innovative research idea with the potential to solve real-world challenges? Submit your project for the Innovative Research Project Pitch Session and get feedback from leading academics and industry experts.
cfc.context: We invite researchers, faculty members, PhD students, engineers, and innovators to submit their most promising research projects. Selected participants will present their projects before a distinguished panel of senior researchers, industry leaders, and innovation stakeholders.
objectives: Foster collaboration between academia and industry.
Identify projects with strong technology transfer and commercialization potential.
Facilitate networking with industrial partners and research experts.
evaluation: Potential for technology transfer or commercialization
Quality and clarity of the pitch
benefits: Present your work to senior researchers and industry experts.
Receive constructive feedback from a multidisciplinary jury.
Increase the visibility of your research.

imed.bio: General Director (Dean) of ENSIIE, France, and President of TunAISa. A Distinguished Professor of Information Systems, HDR-accredited in Computer and Management Sciences, his research focuses on digital intelligence, digital transformation, and data governance. He previously served as Dean of Faculty at IMT-BS, where he founded the SMART² research group.

narjes.bio: Director of ENSI (Ecole Nationale des Sciences de l’Informatique) and Director of the RIADI Laboratory, University of Manouba, Tunisia. A Professor in the Department of Information Systems and Decision Engineering, she teaches Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence. She holds an engineering diploma from ENSEEIHT Toulouse, a PhD from the University of Toulouse 1, and an HDR from ENSI. Her research focuses on modeling and simulation of complex socio-technical systems, information systems, and multi-agent systems. She was also a Fulbright scholar at the University of California, Irvine.

takoua.bio: Associate Professor at ENISo (National School of Engineers of Sousse), University of Sousse, and a researcher at the SERCOM Laboratory, Polytechnic School of Tunisia, University of Carthage. She holds an engineering degree from ENSIMAG (Grenoble, France), a PhD from Grenoble University, and an HDR from the University of Carthage. Her research focuses on Big Data, IoT, and Cloud Computing. She is also a co-founder of the Horizon School of Digital Technologies in Sousse, and an NVIDIA Ambassador in Generative AI.
